_comment: One grammar point per unit,  shown before the first lesson of that unit.
Hand-authored and deliberately narrow: a single rule the learner can hold in
mind while meeting the unit's vocabulary. Stress marks are combining acutes.
Keep each body to one or two sentences — this is a teaching card,  not a chapter.
Where the rule is a set of endings,  pairs or choices,  put them in `table`
({ columns,  rows },  each row's first cell its label) and keep the body to the
one line the table does not say (the owner,  2026-10-09: no 'wall of text').
The ORDER is the point: spine notes run simple to complex in the sequence the
external courses agree on (docs/grammar-sequence.md),  and a branch note never
uses a case or tense its chapter's spine has not yet introduced.
`form` says what the card teaches in terms the paradigm tables can ask
(core/questions.js formPrompt): a table title with the row and column labels
panel.py writes,  or a drill the practice screen already has. A branch card
without one inherits its chapter's; the Cases drill asks only for the cells
the route so far has named.

core1.title: No “a”, no “the”, no “is”
core1.body: Russian has no articles, and it leaves out the present tense of “to be”.

core2.title: Two verb patterns
core2.body: A verb's ending changes with who does it, in one of two sets.

core3.title: Every noun has a gender
core3.body: The ending tells the gender, and words that describe a noun take it. Words for men in -а (па́па) are masculine.

core4.title: Making things plural
core4.body: The plural ending follows the noun's own ending. After к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч it is -и, never -ы.

rows: к г х ж ш щ ч

core5.title: Saying where something is
core5.body: After в or на meaning “in” or “on”, the noun takes the prepositional case.

core6.title: The accusative marks the object
core6.body: The thing an action is done to goes into the accusative.

core7.title: The past tense agrees with the subject
core7.body: Drop -ть and add an ending for the subject's gender and number, not its person. Verbs in -ти have their own stem (идти́ → шёл).

core8.title: Two aspects of every verb
core8.body: Imperfective verbs describe the process or a repeated action; perfective verbs describe one completed act.

core9.title: Talking about the future
examples: I will be working at home.

core10.title: Asking someone to do something
core10.body: Take the они́ form, drop its ending, and add one by what is left. Add -те for вы.

family.title: “My” follows the person you mean
family.body: Learn them as pairs for now; the reason comes with gender in chapter 3.

time.title: Numbers change the noun after them
time.body: The noun after a number changes. Learn the three as set phrases; the case behind them comes in chapter 7.

food.title: Saying what you want
food.body: What you want comes straight after it. Learn the six by heart: хоте́ть follows no single pattern.

school.title: Three ways to “study”
school.body: Russian has three verbs where English has one.

home.title: Asking yes or no
home.body: A yes-or-no question uses the same words in the same order as the statement; only the voice rises, on the word being asked about.

clothes.title: Adjectives in the plural
clothes.body: In the plural an adjective has one ending whatever the gender.

rows: к г х ж ш щ ч

city.title: “This shop” and “This is a shop”
city.body: Before a noun, “this” agrees with it. On its own, э́то means “this is”, whatever the gender.

travel.title: Two verbs for “go”
travel.body: Two verbs for going on foot, by the kind of trip.
examples: I am going to the shop.
Я хожу́ в магази́н ка́ждый день.
I go to the shop every day.

body.title: What hurts is the subject
body.body: Russian says “by me hurts the head” — the aching part is the subject, and the person comes after у: у меня́, у неё.

nature.title: Where in nature
nature.body: A few short masculine nouns take a stressed -у́ instead of -е after в and на: в лесу́, в снегу́, на берегу́. Open spaces take на rather than в: на мо́ре, на у́лице.

work.title: Having and not having
work.body: Not having is the genitive's first job.

animals.title: Living things take the genitive as object
animals.body: For masculine animate nouns — and all animate plurals — the accusative copies the genitive.

emotion.title: Liking is done “to” you
emotion.body: нра́виться puts the person in the dative and the thing liked in the nominative — literally “to me is pleasing”.

speech.title: Speaking a language
speech.body: по- with a language's -ски form says which language you speak, read or understand in, and it never changes: по-ру́сски.

military.title: “With” takes the instrumental
military.body: с plus the instrumental means together with — including who you are fighting or negotiating with.
examples: He is speaking with a friend.

tech.title: Can and want, plus a verb
tech.body: мочь and хоте́ть take a verb in its dictionary form after them: я могу́ де́лать, ты хо́чешь посмотре́ть.
examples: Do you want to watch the video?

sport.title: Playing games vs playing instruments
sport.body: The preposition, and the case after it, say what kind of playing.

art.title: Talking about a work
art.body: о (об before a vowel) plus the prepositional case means “about”.

politics.title: Quantity words take the genitive
politics.body: After мно́го, ма́ло, ско́лько and similar words the noun goes into the genitive: plural for things you count, singular for things you measure.

medicine.title: At the doctor's
medicine.body: “At” a person and “at” a place are said differently.

business.title: How much does it cost?
business.body: сто́ит for one thing, сто́ят for several, then the price.

law.title: What someone is, was, or became
law.body: After рабо́тать, стать and the past of быть, the role goes into the instrumental: юри́ст → юри́стом, судья́ → судьёй.

science.title: Studying a subject
science.body: занима́ться takes the subject or activity in the instrumental, with no preposition: занима́ться матема́тикой, нау́кой.

religion.title: Believing in
religion.body: With в or without it, a different meaning and case.
